title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Social Media Misconduct
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal creates an anonymous Twitter account and routinely posts derogatory comments about specific WSIB adjudicators, calling them "biased hacks" whenever the paralegal loses a case. The LSO discovers the account belongs to the paralegal. Is this misconduct?
options: No, because the account is anonymous and therefore not linked to their professional practice.
No, because paralegals enjoy the right to criticize the government under the Charter.
Yes, paralegals have a duty to encourage respect for the administration of justice, and anonymous, disparaging public attacks violate this duty.
Yes, but only if the adjudicator's actual names are used.
questions.explain: Rule 2.01 specifies that a paralegal shall encourage public respect for the administration of justice. Launching baseless, derogatory public attacks against adjudicators—even anonymously—undermines the legal system and constitutes professional misconduct.
